items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: I knew him when he first came to California. I also knew his first wife very well, and he used to rehearse with the big band at my home.

ctx.x: Yeah, it was a small room upstairs, you know, and Gastel seemingly had some connections with this room, and he sort of used it as a showcase for his artists, you know, to break in. Because I had already recorded, and he booked me, got me booked into this little Beaux Cards room, and it was a small room, very small room, very intimate. And I think that was the first time I met Maria Cole. So Maria Cole, Nat introduced her to me. That was before they got married, of course. And when she wrote this -- when the book…

piano furiously. This is the statement she said, that Carlos Gastell walked over to the gentlemen who owned the club, which were two French brothers and said, "Who is the woman playing the piano?" So they told him, gave him my name. This was what she said, which was not true at all. I don't know why I should have even come into the picture, because it wasn't necessary to even mention my name. The story was Nat King Cole's autobiography, you know, so it really wasn't necessary, unless you could add or say…

But Mrs. Cole went on to state that Carlos Gastell asked how much was I being paid, and this proprietor of the club -- this is in this autobiograph -- says, "How much are you paying her?" So the proprioetor says, "We are paying her $125.00 a week." And said, Gastell went over to Mart Ruby who at that time was his assistant -- he also was a road manager.
